questions.question: A 68-year-old man has fatigue, microcytic anemia, and low ferritin without visible bleeding. What is the best general approach?
choices: Give iron indefinitely without further assessment
Treat the deficiency and evaluate for occult blood loss or impaired absorption
Assume anemia of aging
Order only a repeat hemoglobin in one year
questions.explanation: Low ferritin with microcytosis supports iron deficiency. Treatment should replace iron while identifying the cause, including occult GI loss or malabsorption when appropriate.

questions.question: A patient has thrombocytopenia, anemia, confusion, kidney injury, elevated LDH, and schistocytes. What is the safest next step?
choices: Routine follow-up in one month
Treat as uncomplicated ITP
Arrange emergency hematology evaluation for thrombotic microangiopathy
Prescribe oral iron alone
questions.explanation: Thrombocytopenia plus microangiopathic hemolysis and organ dysfunction suggests TTP or another thrombotic microangiopathy. This is a time-critical hematologic emergency.

questions.question: An unexpected platelet count is 38,000/µL in an asymptomatic patient, and the analyzer reports platelet clumping. What should occur early in the evaluation?
choices: Diagnose ITP immediately
Confirm the count with smear review and an appropriate repeat specimen
Begin anticoagulation
Ignore the result permanently
questions.explanation: EDTA-related clumping can produce pseudothrombocytopenia. Confirm an unexpected result while assessing the patient for any bleeding or clinical instability.

questions.question: A chemotherapy patient has temperature 38.3°C and ANC 300/µL without a clear source. What is the best response?
choices: Wait until a source becomes obvious
Routine clinic follow-up in 48 hours
Urgent febrile-neutropenia evaluation with cultures and prompt empiric therapy
Use an antipyretic as the only treatment
questions.explanation: Profound neutropenia can conceal local inflammatory findings. Fever in this context is an emergency requiring rapid cultures, antimicrobial treatment, and risk-based disposition.

questions.question: Which statement about D-dimer is most accurate?
choices: A positive result proves VTE
A negative result excludes VTE in every patient
Its value depends on pretest probability and an appropriate diagnostic pathway
It replaces imaging in hemodynamically unstable PE
questions.explanation: D-dimer is sensitive but nonspecific. It is most useful to exclude VTE in appropriately selected low-risk patients and should not replace urgent imaging or treatment pathways in high-risk disease.

questions.question: An older adult with dysuria is confused, hypotensive, tachypneic, and mottled but has temperature 37.7°C. Which interpretation is safest?
choices: Sepsis is excluded without high fever
This may be septic shock and requires immediate emergency treatment
Wait for a urine culture before escalating
Confusion is expected with aging
questions.explanation: Suspected infection with hypotension, altered mental status, tachypnea, and poor perfusion indicates sepsis with shock physiology. Older adults may not mount high fever.

questions.question: Which laboratory concept best helps distinguish decreased red-cell production from blood loss or hemolysis?
choices: Platelet count alone
Reticulocyte response interpreted in context
INR alone
D-dimer alone
questions.explanation: An appropriate reticulocyte response suggests the marrow is responding to loss or destruction; an inadequate response supports deficient substrate, suppression, kidney disease, or marrow dysfunction.

questions.question: A transfusion recipient develops fever, dyspnea, and hypotension shortly after the unit begins. What is the first action?
choices: Increase the transfusion rate
Stop the transfusion, assess the patient, and notify the transfusion service
Give an antipyretic and continue unchanged
Discard documentation of the unit
questions.explanation: Suspected transfusion reaction requires immediate cessation of the transfusion, stabilization, identity verification, and transfusion-service notification according to protocol.

questions.question: Which finding should raise concern for a hematologic malignancy despite a normal total white-cell count?
choices: A single normal CBC with no symptoms
Blasts on smear with anemia, thrombocytopenia, and constitutional symptoms
Brief leukocytosis after exercise
Stable mild eosinophilia during seasonal allergies
questions.explanation: Acute leukemia can occur without marked total leukocytosis. Blasts, multiple cytopenias, bleeding, infection, bone pain, or constitutional symptoms require urgent evaluation.

questions.question: Which plan best demonstrates antimicrobial stewardship after empiric treatment is started for a serious infection?
choices: Continue broad therapy indefinitely
Reassess source, cultures, response, organ function, source control, and opportunities to narrow or stop therapy
Ignore culture quality
Add antibiotics whenever fever persists without reassessing the diagnosis
questions.explanation: Stewardship includes correct initial therapy plus repeated reassessment, source control, dose and organ-function review, culture interpretation, and narrowing or discontinuation when supported.
